Rashi on Zevachim 2a:6:1.hebrew: למה לי למיתני אלא: להאריך בלשונו, ליתני ולא עלו לבעלים וכולי, לשון קצרה, כדקיימא לן (פסחים דף ג עמוד ב): לעולם ישנה אדם לתלמידו דרך קצרה.
Rashi on Zevachim 2a:6:1.english: Why do I need to teach 'but': to lengthen its language? Let it teach "and they did not satisfy the owners, etc." in a short form, as we hold (Pesachim 3b): A person should always teach their student in a concise way.

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:10:1.hebrew: הא סתמא [ולשם] פסח - תחילה שחטה סתם, וסופה לשם פסח — כשר, ולא מיפסיל משום תחילתה. אלמא, סתמא כלשמן:
Rashi on Zevachim 2b:10:1.english: But without specification [and for the sake of] a Paschal offering - [If] initially he slaughtered it without specification and its end [was] for the sake of a Paschal offering, it is fit, and it is not disqualified on account of its beginning. Evidently, [slaughtering] without specification is as [slaughtering] for its own sake.

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:12:1.hebrew: א"נ איידי כו' - כלומר, לעולם לא תידוק מיניה: הא סתמא ולשם פסח כשר; דלעולם אימא לך: פסול, דסתמא כשלא לשמו. והאי דקתני לשם שלמים — איידי דפריש בלשמן ולא לשמן לשם שלמים, דהתם דווקא הוא, דאילו סתמא הוי כשר, דעל דעת ראשונה הוא עושה — פריש נמי תנא דמתני' בשלא לשמו ולשמו לשם שלמים ולשם פסח, ולאו דווקא; דה"ה לסתמא ולשם פסח, דמיפסל בתחילת שחיטה:
Rashi on Zevachim 2b:12:1.english: Alternatively, since, etc. - That is to say: Actually, do not infer from it: "Behold, [if slaughtered initially] without specification and [then] for the sake of a Paschal offering, it is fit"; for I could always tell you that it is unfit, because [slaughtering] without specification is like [slaughtering] not for its sake. And as for that which [the Mishnah] teaches: "for the sake of a peace offering" — since it specified "for the sake of a peace offering" in [the clause of] "for their sake and not for their sake," where there it is precise, for had it been without specification it would be fit, since a person acts based on his initial intent, the tanna of our Mishnah also specified in [the clause of] "not for their sake and for their sake": "for the sake of a peace offering and for the sake of a Paschal offering"; and [this is] not precise, for the same law applies to [slaughtering] without specification and [then] for the sake of a Paschal offering, that it is disqualified by the beginning of the slaughter.

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:13:1.hebrew: לשם ששה דברים - משנה בפרק ב"ש, ומקראי יליף להו:
Rashi on Zevachim 2b:13:1.english: For the sake of six matters - [This is] a mishna in the chapter [entitled] Beit Shammai, and [the Gemara] derives them from verses.

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:13:2.english: For the sake of the offering - For the sake of that which it was consecrated [as].

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:13:3.hebrew: לשם זובח - שיתכפר בו בעליו, ולא שיתכפר בו אחר:
Rashi on Zevachim 2b:13:3.english: For the sake of the one sacrificing - That its owner should achieve atonement through it, and not that another should achieve atonement through it.

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:13:4.english: For the sake of the Name - (To provide satisfaction) to the Holy One, Blessed be He, Who spoke (and His will was done).

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:13:5.hebrew: לשם אשים - להקטירם, ולא לעשותם צלי על המזבח — קרבוניי"ש בלע"ז:
Rashi on Zevachim 2b:13:5.english: For the sake of the fires - To burn them [as a fire-offering], and not to make them roasted meat on the altar — carbonées [meat broiled on coals] in Old French.

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:13:6.hebrew: לשם ריח - לאפוקי איברים שצלאן והעלן, דשוב אין בהן ריח. והכי מפרש להו התם:
Rashi on Zevachim 2b:13:6.english: For the sake of aroma - To exclude limbs that one roasted and [then] offered up, as there is no longer an aroma in them; and so [the Gemara] explains them there.

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:1:1.hebrew: נדר הוא - דהא "כאשר נדרת" כתיב, ויש חילוק בין נדר לנדבה: נדר — דאמר "הרי עלי", ונדבה — "הרי זו":
Rashi on Zevachim 2b:1:1.english: It is a vow - For behold, "as you vowed" is written, and there is a difference between a vow and a freewill offering: a vow [is when] one says, "Behold, [it is incumbent] upon me," and a freewill offering [is when one says], "Behold, this [one]."

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:1:2.english: If you did what you vowed - That he performed its services for its own sake.

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:1:3.english: It shall be a vow - And this shall count toward your vow.

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:1:4.hebrew: ואם לאו יהא לנדבה - כאילו התנדבת לזה נדבה אחרת, ולא לשם הראשונה:
Rashi on Zevachim 2b:1:4.english: And if not, it shall be a gift offering - As though you pledged this as another voluntary gift offering, and not for the sake of the original [vow].

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:2:1.hebrew: ונדבה מי שרי לשנויי בה - וכיון דרחמנא קרייה נדבה, מי שרי לשנויי בה? הא אמרינן בפ' שני (לקמן זבחים ד' כט:): אסור לחשב בקדשים, ויליף מקרא ד"לא יחשב". והכי מידרש קרא: אם "מוצא שפתיך תשמור ועשית" - אז יהיה "נדר אשר נדרת", ואם לאו - "נדבה":
Rashi on Zevachim 2b:2:1.english: And is it permitted to deviate in [the sacrifice of] a gift offering? - And [just] because the Merciful One called it a gift offering, is it permitted to deviate in it?! But don't we say in the second chapter (below, Zevachim 29b): It is forbidden to have [improper] intent concerning consecrated offerings, and [the Gemara] derives [this] from the verse, "It shall not be credited" (Leviticus 7:18)? And this is how the verse is expounded: If "that which has gone out of your lips you shall observe and do" (Deuteronomy 23:24), then it shall be "a vow that you have vowed," and if not, [it shall be] "a gift offering."

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:3:1.english: (Received from oral tradition in Menachot, until here.)

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:3:2.hebrew: לא הוית גבן באורתא בתחומא - כלומר: חבל על שלא היית אמש בשבת אצלנו בתוך התחום, שתוכל לבא לבית המדרש ולשמוע:
Rashi on Zevachim 2b:3:2.english: You were not with us in the evening within the [Shabbat] limit - That is to say: What a pity that you were not with us yesterday evening on Shabbat within the [Shabbat] limit, so that you could come to the study hall and hear [it].

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:3:3.english: Bei Ḥarmakh - The name of a place.

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:3:4.english: And resolved them - And resolved them.

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:4:1.english: Not for their sake - [This] implies that he explicitly uprooted their designation.

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:5:1.hebrew: שלא לשם אשה - האשה הזאת, שנכתב לשום אחרת ששמה כשם זו — פסול, דכתיב: "וכתב לה" — לשמה:
Rashi on Zevachim 2b:5:1.english: Not for the sake of a woman - [Meaning, not for the sake of] this woman, [such as] where it was written for the sake of another [woman] whose name is identical to this one's, [it is] invalid, as it is written: "And he shall write for her" — for her sake.

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:5:2.hebrew: וסתמא נמי פסול - כגון אם כתבו הסופר [סתם] לשם לאה, שיהא מזומן לכשיבא אדם אצלו ששמו ושם אשתו (שוין) כן, ויתננו לו. ולקמן מפרש מנלן ממתני' דסתם פסול:
Rashi on Zevachim 2b:5:2.english: And without specification it is also invalid - For example, if the scribe wrote it [without specification] for the name of Leah, so that it would be ready for when a man whose name and his wife's name are so (identical) should come to him, and he would give it to him. And later [the Gemara] explains from where in the Mishnah [we derive] that [a bill of divorce written] without specification is invalid.

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:6:1.hebrew: ושני - ותריץ רבא גופיה, דרמינהו אהדדי:
Rashi on Zevachim 2b:6:1.english: And [he] resolved - And Rava himself, who had raised them as a contradiction against one another, resolved [it].

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:6:2.hebrew: בסתמן לשמן עומדין - הילכך, כל כמה דלא עקר שמייהו בהדיא, הוו לשמן:
Rashi on Zevachim 2b:6:2.english: In their unspecified state they stand for their own sake - Therefore, as long as he did not explicitly uproot their designation, they are [considered slaughtered] for their own sake.

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:7:1.hebrew: מנלן - ממתני', היכי שמע ליה רבא דתיקשה ליה:
Rashi on Zevachim 2b:7:1.english: From where do we [derive this] - From our Mishnah, how did Rava infer it, that it should pose a difficulty to him?

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:7:2.english: That were slaughtered not for their sake - [This] implies that he uprooted their designation from them.

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:7:3.hebrew: שלא נזבחו לשמן - משמע שלא הזכיר שמן עלייהו, דהיינו סתמא:
Rashi on Zevachim 2b:7:3.english: That were not slaughtered for their sake - [This] implies that he did not mention their name upon them, which is [slaughter] without specification.

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:7:4.english: That was written not for the sake of this woman - This implies that it was written explicitly for the sake of another [woman].

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:8:1.english: How [are offerings slaughtered] for their sake, etc. - It is a mishna [below, 13a].

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:8:2.english: For the sake of a Paschal offering and for the sake of a peace offering - This is what he intended regarding it.

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:8:3.hebrew: הא לשם פסח וסתמא - שלא חישב אחריו לשם שלמים — כשר, ואע"ג דסוף שחיטה סתמא אישתחיט:
Rashi on Zevachim 2b:8:3.english: But for the sake of a Paschal offering and without specification - Where he did not have intent afterward for the sake of a peace offering, [it is] fit, even though the end of the slaughter was slaughtered without specification.

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:8:4.hebrew: אלמא סתמן כלשמן דמי - דאי כשלא לשמן דמי, הויא ליה כאילו אמר לשם פסח ולשם שלמים:
Rashi on Zevachim 2b:8:4.english: Apparently, [slaughtering] without specification is considered as for their sake - For if it were considered as [slaughtering] not for their sake, it would be for him as though he said: "For the sake of a Paschal offering and for the sake of a peace offering."

Rashi on Zevachim 2b:9:1.hebrew: על דעת [ראשונה - אבל] היכא דשחטיה כוליה סתמא, אימא לך דפסול:
Rashi on Zevachim 2b:9:1.english: With [his] original intent - [But] where he slaughtered it entirely without specification, I could say to you that it is invalid.

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Zevachim 2b:3.english: Rava’s discourse was on Shabbat night, and Rav Pappa was not able to attend because he was outside the Shabbat limit (Rashi).

Steinsaltz comment #2 on Zevachim 2b:3.english: This Aramaic expression generally refers to the statements of the Sages that were cited in the study hall. In several places in the Talmud, a Sage is cited as having requested that another Sage tell him the superior statements (*mili me'alyata*) of a certain Sage, e.g., Rav, Rav Ḥisda, or Rav Yosef, that were mentioned in the study hall. In other places it is stated that a Sage requested of his colleagues that certain superior statements be attributed to him. A Sage who was absent from the study hall was liable to miss superior statements that were conveyed at the time.

Steinsaltz comment #3 on Zevachim 2b:3.english: A Shabbat limit is the border of a Jewish settlement or of the temporary residence of one or more Jews, determined at the onset of Shabbat. It is defined as two thousand cubits outside the residence. By rabbinic decree it is not permitted for a person to travel on Shabbat beyond this limit. On Shabbat Sages would leave their cities to deliver lectures and sermons in nearby villages. One’s ability to learn Torah on Shabbat was often dependent on his ability to travel to the locale to which the Sage would come without going beyond the Shabbat limit.

Steinsaltz comment #4 on Zevachim 2b:3.english: This city, also called Ḥarmakh, or according to other readings, Harman or Bei Harman, was located on the Shanvata River. Some propose that the source of the name is the Persian word harman, meaning granary.

Steinsaltz comment #5 on Zevachim 2b:3.english: Round wicker barrels were often used as beehives in antiquity. In modern Hebrew, the word kavveret means beehive.

Steinsaltz on Zevachim 2b:3.english: Ravina said to Rav Pappa: Since you were not with us last night within the Shabbat limit of Bei Ḥarmakh, Rav Pappa did not hear that Rava raises a contradiction between two superior Mishnayot and teaches their resolution.

Tosafot on Zevachim 2b:1:1.hebrew: ואם לאו יהא נדבה - אע"ג דבפ"ק דר"ה (דף ו.) דריש ליה לענין בל תאחר, דלא שייך לאחר שחיטה — הכא דריש מפשטיה דקרא, דמשמע דקרי ליה לנדר נדבה:
Tosafot on Zevachim 2b:1:1.english: "And if not, it shall be a voluntary gift" - Even though in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah (6a) [the Gemara] expounds it with regard to the matter of [the prohibition] "you shall not delay" [bal te’aḥer], which does not apply after slaughtering, here it expounds [it] from the plain sense of the verse, which implies that it calls a vow [offering] a voluntary gift [offering].

Tosafot on Zevachim 2b:6:1.hebrew: זבחים בסתם לשמן הן עומדין - ואינו פסול עד שיכוין שלא לשמן. [וא"ת: בפ"ק דחולין (דף יב:) בעי ר"י אי קטן יש לו מחשבה וכו', ופי' בקונטרס: כגון בשחיטת קדשים, דיליף בריש זבחים דבעי לשמה, ושחט קטן עולה לשמה — מי הוי כוונה או לא? הא משמע הכא דמסתמא נמי כשר, ואינו פסול עד שיכוין שלא לשמן!] וי"ל: דסתמא דקטן גרע, דאין לו דעת להבין שהן קדשים, וסבור שהן חולין, והוה ליה מתעסק ופסול, כדאמר בפרק בית שמאי (לקמן זבחים דף מו:): "לשם חולין כשירין, משום חולין פסולה". והאי קטן, אפילו אומר: "יודע אני שהן קדשים ולשמן אני מתכוין" — מיבעיא לן אי כוונתו כוונה, או דילמא לא מהני אם אין מעשיו מוכיחין:
Tosafot on Zevachim 2b:6:1.english: Ordinary slaughtered offerings stand [designated] for their own sake - And [an offering] is not disqualified unless one intends [for it to be] not for its sake. [And if you say: In the first chapter of Chullin (12b), Rabbi Yochanan inquires whether a minor has [legally effective] intention, etc., and the commentary [Rashi] explained: "Such as in the slaughter of sacrificial offerings, where it is derived at the beginning of Zevachim that [slaughter] requires [intention] for its sake, and a minor slaughtered a burnt offering for its sake — is [his thought] considered [valid] intention or not?" But does it not imply here that [an offering slaughtered] with no specified intention is also valid, and it is not disqualified unless one intends [for it to be] not for its sake?] And it can be answered: The default [slaughter] of a minor is worse, for he lacks the understanding to comprehend that they are consecrated offerings and assumes that they are non-sacred [animals]. Therefore, he is [considered] an inadvertent actor (mit'asek), and [the offering] is disqualified, as [the Gemara] states in the chapter [entitled] Beit Shammai (below, Zevachim 46b): "[Slaughtered] for the sake of non-sacred [animals], they are valid; [slaughtered under the assumption that it is] a non-sacred [animal], it is disqualified." And regarding this minor, even if he says, "I know that they are consecrated offerings, and I am intending for their sake" — it was an inquiry for us whether his intention is [valid] intention, or perhaps it is not effective if his actions do not prove [his intention].

Tosafot on Zevachim 2b:6:2.hebrew: סתם אשה לאו לגירושין עומדת - ואפי' זינתה תחת בעלה, מכל מקום לאו להתגרש בגט זה עומדת, וגם אם לא ירצה הבעל לא יגרשנה, אלא שלא תשמשנו. ומתוך הא מילתא מיתרצא מה שמקשים בסוף פרק שני דגיטין (דף כג.): דאמר עובד כוכבים אדעתא דנפשיה עביד ואינו כשר לכתוב את הגט, ובפ' שני דעבודה זרה (דף כו:) אמרי': "ימול ארמאי ואל ימול כותי משום דכותי מתכוין לשם הר גריזים", [והתם נמי] בעינן לשמה כדדרשינן (שם דף כז.) מלה' המול (ימול), ואפי' הכי מכשרינן ארמאי? דיש לחלק בין גט למילה כמו שמחלק כאן בין זבחים לגט: הא סתמא פסול משום דסתם אשה לאו לגירושין קיימא, ולכך נמי [בעובד כוכבים] פסול אע"ג דעביד סתם; אבל מילה סתמא לשמה קיימא כמו זבחים, הילכך עובד כוכבים כשר אע"ג דעביד סתם:
Tosafot on Zevachim 2b:6:2.english: An ordinary woman does not stand [designated] for divorce - And even if she committed adultery while married to her husband, nevertheless she does not stand to be divorced with this [specific] bill of divorce; and furthermore, if the husband does not wish [to do so], he does not divorce her, but rather [he may simply ensure] that she does not engage in marital relations with him. And through this matter, that which is questioned at the end of the second chapter of Gittin (23a) is resolved: where [the Gemara] says that a non-Jew acts with his own intent in mind and is not fit to write a bill of divorce, yet in the second chapter of Avodah Zarah (26b) we say, "An Aramaean [gentile] may circumcise, but a Samaritan may not circumcise, because a Samaritan intends [it] for the sake of Mount Gerizim" — and there, too, we require [circumcision to be performed] for its own sake, as we derive (ibid. 27a) from "unto the Lord... he shall be circumcised" [or: "he shall surely be circumcised"] — and even so we validate an Aramaean? For one can distinguish between a bill of divorce and circumcision just as [the Gemara] distinguishes here between slaughtered offerings and a bill of divorce: this [bill of divorce written] without specification is invalid because an ordinary woman does not stand [designated] for divorce, and therefore in [the case of] a non-Jew it is also invalid even though he acts without specification; but circumcision by default stands [designated] for its own sake, like slaughtered offerings; therefore, a non-Jew is valid even though he acts without specification.

Tosafot on Zevachim 2b:8:1.hebrew: הא לשם פסח וסתמא כשר - פי' בקונטרס: דסוף שחיטה סתמא אישתחיט. ותימה: כיון דאמר בתחילת שחיטה "לשם פסח", וכי כל שעה יש לו לדבר עד שיגמר שחיטתו?! ונראה לפרש, דבשתי עבודות איירי — כגון דשחיט לשם פסח וקיבל סתם. ומיהו, בפרק תמיד נשחט (פסחים דף נט:) מיבעי לן: אי בעבודה אחת תנן, או בשתי עבודות? ועבודה אחת היינו כדפירש הקונטרס. ויש ליישב, דאפילו אם תימצי לומר "לשם פסח וסתמא" פסול — [אפ"ה] אין צריך לדבר כל שעה, אלא שבתחילת שחיטה יאמר שעושה כל השחיטה לשם שחיטת פסח:
Tosafot on Zevachim 2b:8:1.english: "But [if he slaughters it] for the sake of a Paschal offering and without specification, it is fit" - Rashi explained that the end of the slaughter was performed without specification. And this is astonishing: Since he stated at the beginning of the slaughter "for the sake of a Paschal offering," must he speak continuously until his slaughtering is completed?! And it appears [preferable] to explain that [the Mishnah] is dealing with two services, such as where he slaughtered for the sake of a Paschal offering and received [the blood] without specification. However, in the chapter [entitled] Tamid Nishchat (Pesachim 59b), we raise the dilemma: Did we learn [the Mishnah regarding] one service, or regarding two services? And one service is as Rashi explained. And it can be resolved that even if you were to say that [slaughtering] "for the sake of a Paschal offering and without specification" is unfit, [nevertheless] he does not need to speak continuously; rather, at the beginning of the slaughter he should state that he is performing the entire slaughter for the sake of the slaughter of a Paschal offering.

Zevachim 2b:3.english: Ravina said to Rav Pappa: Since you were not with us last night within the Shabbat limit of Bei Ḥarmakh, you did not hear that Rava raises a contradiction between two superior Mishnayot and teaches their resolution.
